Analyst summary:
**Investigation summary – Dow Chemical (disruption first reported ≈ 25 Aug 2017)**  

| Tier | Company (sector) | Structural relationship to Dow (down‑stream or alternative supplier) | Evidence found in this investigation* |
|------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Tier 1** | Avient (specialty polymer compounds & colourants) | Direct downstream customer of Dow’s advanced materials business. | No filing or corpus mention linking the 2017 disruption to Avient. |
|  | Grupo Pochteca (industrial chemicals distributor) | Down‑stream distributor of Dow‐produced bulk chemicals. | None. |
|  | Nan Ya Plastics (PVC & polyester plastics) | Uses Dow’s polymer resins as feedstock. | None. |
|  | HDC Hyundai Engineering Plastics (engineering‑plastic compounds) | Direct consumer of Dow’s specialty polymers. | None. |
|  | **Hyundai Motor** (passenger vehicles) | Major automotive customer for a range of Dow plastics, coatings and performance chemicals used in vehicle interiors, exteriors and power‑train components. | No SEC filing found for Hyundai Motor; the corpus search returned only unrelated Posco text – no explicit reference to a Dow‑related disruption. |
|  | Samsung Electronics (automotive electronics & displays) | Uses Dow‑derived chemicals for semiconductor packaging, display glass and battery materials. | No direct evidence located. |
|  | Toray Industries (carbon‑fiber composites & engineering resins) | Competes with/uses Dow’s high‑performance resin portfolio. | None. |
|  | Saudi Arabian Oil (crude & petroleum products) – indirect supplier of feedstock to Dow. | No specific evidence of impact. |
|  | Formosa Plastics (PVC resin, epichlorohydrin) | Down‑stream user of Dow’s PVC and epoxy chemicals. | None. |
| **Tier 2** (selected high‑profile downstreams / alternative suppliers) | Valeo SE (automotive lighting & ADAS) – uses Dow plastics/coatings. | No evidence found. |
|  | Nexen Tire, Bridgestone, Michelin‑type tire makers – use Dow rubber additives. | No evidence found. |
|  | ZF TRW Automotive (airbags, safety systems) – uses Dow polymers for seals & foams. | No evidence found. |
|  | Tokai Rika (automotive switches/seatbelts) – Dow polymer components. | No evidence found. |
|  | BAIC BluePark New Energy (EVs) – Dow battery‑material chemicals. | No evidence found. |
|  | Exxon Mobil, Shell (refined fuels & lubricants) – both supply feedstock to Dow and buy downstream products. | No evidence found. |
|  | BASF SE, Lanxess, Asahi Kasei, etc. – competing chemical producers that could be alternative suppliers for customers of Dow. | No evidence found. |
|  | Major OEMs (Volkswagen, Mercedes‑Benz, Toyota Motor, Honda, Kia, Stellantis, Tesla) – all consume Dow’s plastics, coatings or performance chemicals in vehicle manufacturing. | No filing or corpus reference linking the Aug 2017 event to any of these firms. |
|  | Battery‑cell makers (LG Energy Solution, Panasonic, Samsung SDI, CATL‑type) – use Dow‑derived electrolyte additives and separator materials. | No evidence found. |
|  | Apple (consumer electronics) – uses Dow chemicals in device casings & displays. | No evidence found. |

\* **Evidence sources used**  
1. **`traverse_supply_graph`** – identified the full set of downstream customers and alternative suppliers up to two tiers away from Dow (79 enriched companies, 320 reachable). This provides the structural risk map.  
2. **`search_corpus`** – free‑text queries for “Dow AND Hyundai” and “Dow disruption August 2017”. The only returned hit was a Posco filing that mentions Hyundai HYSCO in an unrelated anti‑trust context; it does not confirm any impact from the Dow event. No other company‑specific filings or narrative references to the 2017 Dow disruption were retrieved.  
3. **`get_supplier_info`** – attempted to pull a filing for Hyundai Motor Company (a key downstream). The system returned “No filings on record”, indicating that no SEC‑type filing was available in the dataset for this company at the requested date.

### What could not be confirmed
* **Direct impact statements** – None of the companies listed above have a filing or corpus excerpt that explicitly mentions being affected by Dow’s August 2017 disruption (e.g., supply shortages, production delays, financial write‑downs).  
* **Quantitative effect** – No disclosed loss amounts, inventory adjustments, or mitigation actions were found in the available documents.  
* **Alternative supplier shifts** – While many Tier‑2 chemical firms (BASF, Lanxess, Asahi Kasei, etc.) could plausibly absorb demand, no evidence was located showing they actually did so because of this event.

### Overall assessment
The structural analysis shows that a very large and diverse set of downstream manufacturers—spanning automotive OEMs, tire makers, electronics producers, battery‑cell companies, oil & gas refiners, and other chemical firms—are **potentially at risk** when Dow experiences a supply disruption. However, within the limited tool budget (four calls) and the data returned, **no concrete public evidence was found that any of these downstreams reported material effects from the specific August 2017 Dow incident**.

### Investigation completeness
*Tool‑call budget used*: 3 out of 4 allowed calls (traverse → 1, search → 2, get_supplier_info → 3).  
*Remaining call*: unused, but per instruction no further calls will be made.  

Because the evidence base does not contain explicit confirmations, the investigation remains **incomplete** with respect to quantifying or qualifying actual downstream impacts. The list above should be treated as a structural risk map; any real‑world impact would need to be verified by additional filings, press releases, or news reports that were not captured in this limited dataset.
